Title: Demo Day
Author: StoryFlow fixtures

INT. CO-WORKING SPACE - NIGHT

Empty desks, one lamp still on. PRIYA (30s, hoodie, three empty coffee cups) stares at a laptop.
MARCUS (40s, rolled-up sleeves) paces behind her with a whiteboard marker.

MARCUS
Run it again. From the top.

PRIYA
We've run it eleven times.

MARCUS
Then twelve is a nice round number.

Priya hits a key. A slide flashes on the wall: "LOOP - Lost things, found."

PRIYA
(flat, exhausted)
Every year, people lose four billion dollars' worth of stuff in taxis, trains and airports.
Loop finds it.

MARCUS
Stop. You sound like you're reading a ransom note.

PRIYA
It's two in the morning, Marcus.

MARCUS
Investors don't care what time it is. They care if you believe it.

Priya closes the laptop slowly.

PRIYA
Do you?

Marcus stops pacing.

MARCUS
I quit a pension for this. What do you think?

INT. CO-WORKING SPACE - KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS

A tiny kitchen with a broken espresso machine. Marcus fills a kettle. Priya leans on the
doorframe.

PRIYA
My mom lost her wedding ring on a bus in 1998. She still checks the lost and found every time
she rides that line.

MARCUS
That's the pitch.

PRIYA
That's my mom.

MARCUS
That's why it's the pitch.

The kettle starts to hiss. Priya pulls out her phone and starts typing notes.

INT. CONFERENCE HALL - DAY

Bright stage lights. Rows of investors with badges. DANA OKAFOR (50s, sharp suit, the lead
judge) checks her watch in the front row.

Priya walks on stage. No slides behind her, just a black screen.

PRIYA
In 1998 my mother lost her wedding ring on the number 14 bus.

Dana looks up from her watch.

PRIYA (CONT'D)
Twenty-six years later, she still checks.

The screen lights up: "LOOP."

DANA
And did she find it?

PRIYA
Not yet. That's why we're here.

Marcus, in the wings, closes his eyes and exhales.
